You use the passive form when you do not know the agent of the sentence or you do not want to mention it.

You can use the passive voice in past simple to talk about actions in the past. You use this tense when you want to focus on the action and not on the person who did the action.
Look at the forms of the passive voice in past simple:

Interrogative:
was / were + verb in p. participle

Example:
What was done to help the customer?

Negative:
was / were + not + verb in p. participle

Example:
Internet was not created until 1969.

Affirmative:
was / were + verb in p. participle
Example:
This Operating System was created in 1995.

Remember you don't have to say who did the action, however you can mention the agent with the preposition by.

images.text:
Brief History of Operating Systems

Operating systems were first created in the middle of the 20th century, they helped to control computers which could be as big as an entire room. Since then, OS have changed the way users approach them, their design, interactivity, and speed among other features. Let's have a review of their major characteristics.
The first generation of Operating Systems was quite experimental. They had a lot of mechanical components and were very big. They needed human operators to configure the hardware as the machine operated and could execute only one program at a time, which took a long time.

The second generation of OS wasn't designed to have one user at a time, it led to a model of ‘modes of operations'. Some users were not allowed to perform all types of actions in the OS, instead, it introduced the basic concepts of administrator and users, and developed transistors and printed circuits.
Why was the third generation known as the multi-programmed Batch Systems? The answer lies on the Small-scale Integrated Circuits, which were used by these OS, they allowed the CPU to run more than one job at a time, interrupting programs while they were waiting for their processes to finish. However, human operators had to pre-read magnetic tapes and run them sequentially.

For almost thirty years, we have had the four generation of OS. The concept of Personal Computer was introduced, and it has provided security and privacy to the user. Also, it has emphasized on the use of multitasking, running many more processes than before but still gaining control on the computer. As time passes by, OS becomes faster and more user-friendly.
